item.title: Junior scholarship exams to begin Dec 8
item.description:
The schedule for this year's Junior Scholarship Examination for class eight students has been published, with the nationwide examination set to begin on December 8 and end on December 15.
The Dhaka Education Board published the examination schedule on its website on Sunday, saying the examinations will generally be held from 10am to 1pm.
According to the schedule, the examination will be held in Bengali on December 8, English on December 10, Mathematics on December 13, and Science and Bangladesh and Global Studies on December 15.
According to special instructions issued for the examinees, they must take their seats in the examination halls at least 30 minutes before the start of the examinations.
The examinations will be conducted according to the time specified on the question papers, it said.
Separate one hour and 30 minutes will be allocated for Science and Bangladesh and Global Studies, meaning a total of three hours will be available for the two subjects.
The examinees have been asked to collect their admit cards from their respective heads of institutions at least seven days before the examination.
They must correctly write and fill in the designated circles on the OMR answer sheets with their roll and registration numbers, subject codes and other required information. The answer sheets must not be folded under any circumstances.
The examinees will be allowed to use board-approved ordinary scientific calculators.
No person other than the centre secretary and examinees will be allowed to bring mobile phones or any electronic devices into the examination centre.

item.title: 2 held over killings of four family members in Rangpur
item.description:
Police arrested two youths early Sunday in connection with the recovery of the bodies of a retired Rangpur Zilla School teacher, his wife and their two children from their home in Machuapara, Kamal Kachna area of Rangpur city.
The accused were identified as Siddhartha Das, 23, and Mugdha Das, 19. They were detained from Dakhiganj cremation ground in the city. Both are residents of Machuapara.
The incident occurred on Thursday night in the area, but police recovered the bodies of the four family members on Saturday night.
The deceased were identified as Ganapati Chakraborty, 65, his wife Pritilata Chakraborty, 50, their daughter Prarthi Chakraborty, 24, a master’s student, and their 12-year-old son Priyam Chakraborty, a Class V student at Rangpur Zilla School.
Meanwhile, hundreds of students of Rangpur Zilla School boycotted classes and staged demonstrations on Sunday, demanding the arrest and death penalty of those responsible for the killings.
They marched to the offices of the Rangpur Metropolitan Police Commissioner and the district administration and submitted separate memorandum demanding the immediate arrest of the suspects and justice.
Later, they held a human chain and demonstration on a main road in front of the school.
At a press conference on Sunday, Rangpur Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mohammad Abdul Mabud said the two suspects had allegedly been consuming yaba on the roof of Ganapati’s house late Thursday night when the retired teacher heard the noise and went upstairs. After seeing them, Ganapati reportedly told them to stop taking drugs. The suspects then allegedly strangled him with a gamcha, or towel.
Hearing his cries, his wife Pritilata and daughter Prarthi came to the rooftop and were also allegedly strangled. The suspects then entered the house and killed Priyam, the couple’s only son, in the same way, the commissioner said.
The suspects allegedly remained inside the house throughout Thursday night. They reportedly showered in the bathroom, ate dates from the dining table and consumed yaba.
They also allegedly soaked the mobile phones of Ganapati and Pritilata in water mixed with washing powder to remove their fingerprints, according to police.
The suspects reportedly stayed inside the house until Friday morning and left when the area became quieter during Friday prayers. They allegedly ransacked the house to make the killings appear to be part of a robbery.
Police said the suspects later hid the stolen gold ornaments in an abandoned area behind a temple near the house. The ornaments were recovered based on information provided by the suspects.
Commissioner Mabud, who became emotional while describing the killings, said the suspects had confessed to killing all four victims after their arrest.
A murder case has been filed in connection with the incident, he added.
Family members and locals said Ganapati had lived in the house with his family after retiring from Rangpur Zilla School. He later practised as a homeopathic doctor.
His sister, Puja Chakraborty, said the family had been unreachable since Thursday night. Despite repeated phone calls, she could not contact Pritilata or any other family member, while all four phones at the house were switched off.
Concerned relatives went to the house on Saturday night and found the main gate locked. After being informed, police and Fire Service personnel arrived at around 10:45pm and broke open the door.
They found one body inside a room and three others near the rooftop area.
The bodies were recovered early Sunday and sent to the Rangpur Medical College Hospital morgue for autopsies.
A Criminal Investigation Department (CID) crime scene team collected evidence and cordoned off the house.
CID Rangpur Superintendent of Police Sumit Chowdhury said investigators initially suspected the incident was linked to a robbery. As the killings had occurred about two days earlier, the bodies had already begun to decompose, he said.

item.title: 'New policy for primary education within a month'
item.description:
State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj on Sunday said a new policy will be formulated within a month to ensure effective management, monitoring and accountability of primary education activities.
"All officials and employees in the primary education sector will discharge their duties in line with the new policy, while activities of government primary schools will also be conducted accordingly," he said.
The state minister was speaking as the chief guest at a daylong training workshop titled "Conducting Class Activities, Monitoring, Accountability and Reform of Administrative Structure in Primary Education of Bangladesh" at the Shilpakala Academy here.
"We will formulate the new policy within a month . . . The primary education family and government primary schools will also be run accordingly," Bobby Hajjaj said.
Highlighting the government's plans for the development of primary education, he said members of the primary education family were working relentlessly to build an educated Bangladesh in line with the prime minister's vision.
He said efforts were underway to ensure that the implementation of the government's electoral pledges becomes visible within a short time.
"The primary education family will be the key force in realising the prime minister's dream for Bangladesh," he said.
Deputy Director of Primary Education in Barisal Division Nilufa Yasmin presided over the workshop.
Director (Planning and Development) of the Directorate of Primary Education Mirajul Islam Ukil and Deputy Secretary (Administration-1) Mohammad Sakhawat Hossain Sarker attended the event as special guests.
Officials and employees from different levels of the primary education sector attended the workshop, where various aspects of classroom activities, monitoring, accountability and reform of the administrative structure were discussed.

item.title: Swapon calls for expanding tree plantation social movement
item.description:
The prime minister's political adviser, Zahir Uddin Swapon, on Sunday called for expanding the ongoing social movement for tree plantation and greening.
He made the call at a discussion organized by the Krishibid Association as part of a tree plantation program at the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute auditorium in Gazipur.
Zahir Uddin Swapon said, “It is our moral responsibility to take care of the environment and ecosystem. For sustenance in the universe, we have to depend on the ecosystem. So, instead of limiting ourselves to mechanical development, we have to work by cultivating intellect and conscience to create a habitable earth for future generations.”
Highlighting the global context of the climate crisis, he said temperatures are rising due to carbon emissions caused by excessive use of fossil fuels. Coastal low-lying areas face the risk of being inundated, he said, adding there is no alternative to greening and afforestation to overcome this global crisis.
Swapon recalled that Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman had taken far-sighted initiatives for environmental conservation and launched the tree plantation movement alongside ensuring food security in the country.
In continuation of that, the present government, under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, has adopted a mega plan to plant 250 million trees over the next five years, he said, adding that this year’s target has already been successfully achieved.
He strongly urged for extensive expansion of greening across the country with the participation of every family, educational institution, and social organization under the concept “One Child, One Tree."
At the same time, he called upon the agriculturalist community to play a leading role in making the social movement a success.
Agriculturist Dr Kamruzzaman Kaiser presided over the program while Nurul Islam Nayan MP, Shahidul Islam Bablu MP, Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture Selim Khan, and leaders of the Krishibid Association spoke on the occasion.

item.title: Bangladesh's Sadia Haque appointed UN advocate for South Asia on women in digital trade
item.description:
Sadia Haque, co-founder and CEO of ShareTrip, has been appointed by the UN Trade and Development (Unctad) as an eTrade for Women Advocate for South Asia for the 2026–27 term.
She is the first Bangladeshi appointed to the role.
The eTrade for Women initiative appoints a small number of women business leaders worldwide to carry the concerns of women digital entrepreneurs into policy discussions with governments and regulators.
Previous advocates have been drawn from Kenya, Egypt, Colombia, Malaysia, Senegal, Nigeria, the Philippines, and India.
In the role, Sadia Haque will represent the region's women-led digital businesses in dialogue on digital trade and the digital economy, and will contribute to the initiative's Masterclasses and community programs across South Asia.
Her designation will be formally announced at Unctad in Geneva in September.
"I'm honoured to take on this role at a time when South Asia's digital economy is creating new opportunities for women entrepreneurs. I know from experience that building a technology business takes more than a good idea, it takes access to networks, capital, knowledge and an ecosystem that gives women the opportunity to lead. I hope to use this platform to bring the experiences of women entrepreneurs in our region into the policy conversation and help make the path easier for those coming next," Sadia Haque said.
She co-founded ShareTrip with Kashef Rahman.
Under her leadership, the platform introduced automatic refunds, date changes, and cancellations, none of which existed in the Bangladeshi market at the time and built the country's largest domestic hotel and resort inventory, bringing hundreds of local properties online for the first time.
ShareTrip became the first superbrand in the travel sector and has also won at the World Travel Awards for six consecutive years, with recognition dating back to 2018.
In addition, Sadia Haque has already received several honours in recognition of her contributions, including the Philip Kotler Awards' "Women Leader of the Year" in 2023, the "ICT Woman of the Year" title at the 9th Brac Bank–The Daily Star ICT Awards in 2024, and "Outstanding Woman in Business" at the 23rd DHL–The Daily Star Bangladesh Business Awards in 2025.

item.title: Guardian Life Insurance holds annual sales conference
item.description:
Guardian Life Insurance Limited celebrated the dedication and achievements of its sales force at the Annual Sales Conference 2026, held under the spirited theme “Odommo Guardian” in Cox’s Bazar.
The conference brought together more than 900 sales leaders and financial advisors from across Bangladesh to celebrate their achievements, recognize outstanding contributions and strengthen camaraderie within Guardian’s sales community.
A key highlight of the event was the recognition of 18 outstanding performers for their exceptional contributions and achievements during the past year.
Tapan Chowdhury, co-founder and sponsor of Guardian, addressed the participants through a video message, saying: “Guardian has reached where it is today because of your relentless effort, dedication, courage and personal sacrifices. You are the real players on the field and the driving force behind every achievement we have made. Today, we have been able to extend insurance protection to more than 13.2 million people, and this is an achievement we can all take pride in. You are the true strength of Guardian, the real heroes of our success, and you are Odommo Guardian.”
Syed Nasim Manzur, sponsor director of Guardian, was present at the conference.
Addressing the gathering, he said: “The trust Guardian has earned over the years stems from the honesty, professionalism and hard work of our people. As Odommo Guardian, our shared goal is to bring every family in Bangladesh under the protection of insurance, and we can move closer to that goal by facing every challenge together with integrity, commitment and determination.”
Sheikh Rakibul Karim, CEO of Guardian Life, said: “At Guardian, our progress is driven by the people who work tirelessly every day. Their commitment, discipline and dedication have shaped our achievements and enabled us to fulfil the promises we make to our customers. This occasion gives us an opportunity to recognize their invaluable contributions and celebrate the people behind our success.”
Mahmudur Rahman Khan, chief retail business officer of Guardian, said: “Our strength in the retail business comes from the relationships our people build with customers every day. By staying close to their needs and earning their trust, we can take insurance protection to more families across the country.”
The conference also featured performance-review sessions and strategic-planning workshops, during which participants reflected on recent progress and discussed the company’s priorities for the year ahead.

item.title: NCC Bank donates ambulance to Zia Heart Foundation, Dinajpur
item.description:
As part of its CSR initiatives, NCC Bank PLC has provided a modern ambulance equipped with medical facilities to Zia Heart Foundation, Dinajpur, to support emergency healthcare services for cardiac patients in the region.
Recently at the Secretariat, in the presence of Prof Dr AZM Zahid Hossain, Minister for Women and Children Affairs and Social Welfare, and Farzana Sharmin, MP, State Minister for Social Welfare, Md Nurun Newaz Salim, chairman of NCC Bank, handed over the keys of the ambulance to AKM Azad, general secretary of Zia Heart Foundation, Dinajpur.
Dr Mohammad Abu Yusuf, secretary, Ministry of Social Welfare; Engineer Abdus Salam, vice chairman, Khairul Alam Chaklader, director and chairman of the executive committee; M Shamsul Arefin, managing director; Md Zakir Anam, additional managing director of NCC Bank; Khalekuzzaman Babu, senior member of the governing board, Anwarul Kabir, treasurer; Prof Shah Alam Ashrafi, development advisor; Syed Mezba Alam, CEO; Md Rafiqul Islam, assistant officer of Zia Heart Foundation, Dinajpur; and other officials from both organizations were present on the occasion.
Speaking at the event, Prof Dr AZM Zahid Hossain, MP, Minister for Women and Children Affairs and Social Welfare appreciated NCC Bank for undertaking the initiative.
He said the government is working to improve the country’s overall healthcare and medical services and emphasized the importance of greater participation by the private sector in strengthening the healthcare system.
He hoped that other corporate organizations would also come forward and play a more active role in CSR initiatives for the welfare of the people.
Md Nurun Newaz Salim, chairman of NCC Bank, said: “Since its inception, NCC Bank has been contributing to the socio-economic development of the country alongside its banking operations. As part of our CSR initiatives, we have been working in various areas, including education, healthcare, support for marginal farmers, financing for agricultural research, assistance to disadvantaged and underprivileged people, development of environmentally friendly ecosystems to improve the livelihoods of people living in char areas, and humanitarian assistance for persons with disabilities. We remain committed to supporting people from different segments of society. As part of these continued efforts, NCC Bank has provided a modern ambulance equipped with medical facilities to Zia Heart Foundation, Dinajpur.”

item.title: Chevron, Asian University for Women conclude Math and Science Summer School 2026
item.description:
The Asian University for Women (AUW) campus in Chittagong recently hosted a ceremony to mark the closing of the 2026 “Math and Science Summer School”.
Supported by Chevron Bangladesh, the program concluded with the awarding of certificates to 104 bright college girls from across the country who had successfully completed the intensive four-week program.
The chief guest of the ceremony was Md Ziauddin, Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong.
Joining him on the dais were distinguished guests including Ashiq Rahman, director of operations, Chevron Bangladesh, and Dee Bourbon, lead advisor community partnerships at Chevron.
Their presence underscored Chevron’s long-standing partnership with AUW and its dedication to building an inclusive education system for women in Bangladesh.
From AUW, Mohiuddin Ahsanul Kabir Chowdhury, director of the Summer School, extended his heartfelt gratitude to the students and faculty for their dedication and hard work, noting that the program continues to serve as a beacon of opportunity for young women across the country.
Ashiq Rahman, director of operations, Chevron Bangladesh, said: "Chevron is proud to support the Math and Science Summer School since 2019. Through initiatives like this, we aim to encourage more young women to pursue STEM education and unlock their potential."
Dee Bourbon, lead advisor, community partnerships, Chevron, said: "We are proud to support a program that helps young women build confidence, expand their knowledge, and pursue opportunities that can shape their futures.
Chief guest Md Ziauddin, Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong, praised AUW and Chevron Bangladesh for their continued commitment to advancing women’s education and preparing future leaders in Stem.
He emphasized that initiatives such as the Summer School play a vital role in shaping the next generation of scientists, innovators and changemakers.
A highlight of the event was the presentation of the "Emerging Woman Leader in Stem” award to nine outstanding participants in recognition of their exceptional performance and leadership potential.
Since its inception in 2019, the Chevron Bangladesh-supported AUW Summer School has given 477 young women from across Bangladesh access to specialized courses in mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer programming, and public health taught by experienced local and international faculty.

item.title: Interspeed Activation, Malaysia’s Lavis to advance Bangladesh’s sports infrastructure
item.description:
Interspeed Activation Ltd recently entered a partnership with Malaysian sports arena management company Lavis Sdn Bhd to explore the development of a modern, world-class sports arena concept in Bangladesh.
The partnership is aligned with Bangladesh’s government’s vision to strengthen sports facilities and create better infrastructure for athletes and the wider sporting community.
Under the agreement, Interspeed and Lavis will work together to develop a concept for a multi-purpose sports arena for the Bangladesh Football Federation and the Ministry of Sports.
The proposed facility is expected to support football as well as other sporting activities and events.
The signing was attended by Adnan Karim, director of Interspeed Activation Ltd, and Datuk Jack Koh of Lavis Sdn Bhd.
Speaking on the occasion, Karim said: “This agreement marks an important step toward strengthening the country’s sporting infrastructure. Together with Lavis, we look forward to developing a facility that can serve athletes, sports federations and the wider sporting community for years to come.”
The concept development will explore the requirements for a modern, multi-purpose arena that can support sports development while also providing a suitable venue for major sporting events and activities.
Operating since 1968, Interspeed Activation Ltd is one of the pioneering advertising and marketing agencies in Bangladesh.
The company works across brand activation, sports partnerships and integrated marketing programs, serving clients across telecommunications, aviation, FMCG, and other sectors.

Markle’s role has not been revealed, and no contract has been signed. Netflix and Markle’s representatives have declined to comment on the reports.
“The Gentlemen," created by Guy Ritchie, stars Theo James as an aristocrat who inherits his late father’s estate and discovers an underground cannabis operation. The second season is scheduled to premiere on September 3.
Markle is best known for playing Rachel Zane in the legal drama "Suits," where she appeared for seven seasons from 2011 to 2018.
She has maintained a production partnership with Netflix through Archewell Productions, which she runs with Prince Harry. Their projects include “With Love, Meghan," “Heart of Invictus," and “Harry & Meghan."
Markle is also set to make a cameo as herself in the upcoming Amazon MGM comedy “Close Personal Friends," starring Brie Larson and Lily Collins.
